meta.landingTitle: {brand}: your family tree, with evidence and in your language
meta.landingDescription: An open-source, Spanish-first family-history platform for Mexican and binational families: a tree built from evidence, stories, interviews and privacy by default. Early access by invitation.

hero.title: Your family's history, with evidence, stories and voices.
hero.lead: Build your tree from civil records and parish books, and keep what no archive holds in the same place: the stories, the photos and the voices of your elders. Spanish first, and under your control.
hero.status: We are building the platform with a small group of families. It is not open to the public yet.

how.title: How it works
how.lead: Four ideas guide everything we build.

tree.title: A tree with evidence
tree.body: Every fact carries its source: the civil record, the baptism entry or the interview it came from. When two sources disagree, both stay and you choose the one you prefer.

stories.title: Stories and interviews
stories.body: Anecdotes, recipes, photos and your grandparents' voices live next to the tree, not in a separate drawer.

privacy.title: Private by default
privacy.body: Living people are visible only inside their family space. You decide who joins and with what permissions.

export.title: Take everything with you
export.body: Your tree is yours. Full export in open formats will always be free, with no conditions.

mexican.title: Made for Mexican families
mexican.lead: Genealogy software usually assumes other customs. This one starts here.

surnames.title: Two surnames
surnames.body: Paternal and maternal surnames, given names and names in use, nicknames. Nobody's surname is forced to change at marriage.

compadrazgo.title: Compadrazgo
compadrazgo.body: Godparents for baptism, confirmation and marriage are recorded on each sacrament; compadres are derived from them.

records.title: Civil records and parish books
records.body: Citations with book, folio and entry, Registro Civil records and oral testimony, each with its own source type.

muertos.title: Día de Muertos
muertos.body: A place to remember those who are gone, with their photos and stories, in the spirit of an ofrenda.

promises.title: Our privacy promises
promises.lead: This is not fine print: it is how the product is designed.

living.title: The living stay private by default
living.body: Nothing about a living person is ever published. Only their family space sees them.

dna.title: No DNA
dna.body: We do not ask for, store or analyse genetic data. We do not ask for the CURP either.

noSale.title: We do not sell data
noSale.body: We do not sell your information or use it to train artificial-intelligence models.

export.title: Free export
export.body: You will be able to download your whole tree as GEDCOM 7, GEDCOM 5.5.1 and JSON, free, whenever you want.

whatIs.question: What is {brand}?
whatIs.answer: It is an open-source, Spanish-first family-history platform for building your family tree from evidence and keeping its stories, photos and interviews in the same place.

access.question: How can I start using it?
access.answer: We are in invitation-only early access with a small group of families. It is not open to the public yet.

living.question: Who can see my living relatives' data?
living.answer: Only the members of your family space. Anyone not recorded as deceased and born within the last 110 years, or with no known birth date, is treated as living and is never published.

dna.question: Do you use DNA or genetic tests?
dna.answer: No. We do not ask for, store or analyse genetic data, and we do not ask for the CURP either.

data.question: Do you sell my data or use it to train artificial intelligence?
data.answer: No. We do not sell data and we do not train models on family content.

export.question: Will I be able to take my tree to another program?
export.answer: Yes. Full export as GEDCOM 7, GEDCOM 5.5.1 and JSON will always be free, for every family.

language.question: Is it available in English?
language.answer: Yes. Mexican Spanish is the primary language and English comes second, with binational families in mind.

openSource.question: Is it open source?
openSource.answer: Yes. The code is published under the AGPL-3.0 licence and anyone can review it.

maker.question: Who makes it?
maker.answer: Innovaciones MADFAM S.A.S. de C.V., a company based in Cuernavaca, Morelos.
